entries.name: Power iteration clustering
entries.definition: A clustering algorithm that uses an early-stopped power iteration of a normalized similarity matrix to embed observations and then applies k-means to their embedding coordinates.
entries.identity_notes: This is the Lin and Cohen ICML 2010 algorithm. Its qualified PIC alias is distinct from path integral clustering: it truncates a matrix iteration to form coordinates instead of merging clusters by resolvent descriptors. It is not a generic eigensolver or a claim that converging to the dominant eigenvector finds clusters. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 218 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 15 lines each in existing discovery/review context. Five neighboring native records and five exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges were inspected.
limitations: The stopping test is a heuristic for a useful intermediate embedding, not a certificate of cluster recovery. A regular graph with degree-proportional initialization starts at a constant vector and can yield no separating coordinates.

Positive row sums are required for the stated row-stochastic normalization. Disconnected graphs, negative eigenmodes and collisions in a one-dimensional embedding limit a blanket spectral or convergence interpretation.

The paper reports experimental tolerance 1e−5/n. The released experiment driver sets baseconv=0.001 and uses baseconv/n, with maxit=5000. These are different settings, not an asserted benchmark reproduction or proof that either setting is wrong.
Choice of similarity, initialization, stopping rule and k-means solution affects the partition. No code was executed, and no runtime, accuracy or global-optimum claim is made.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 2.1–2.4, PDF pp. 1–4; Algorithm 1 and experimental stopping threshold on p. 4

claims.statement: For a symmetric nonnegative similarity matrix A with zero diagonal and positive row sums, form D_ii=sum_j A_ij and W=D^−1 A. Starting with a nonnegative nonzero vector v, iterate v_next=Wv/||Wv||_1. Use an intermediate vector before convergence to the constant dominant right eigenvector. Following Algorithm 1 and the released pic.m, monitor d_next=abs(v_next−v) componentwise and stop when max_i abs(d_next_i−d_i) is sufficiently small, subject to an iteration cap. Apply k-means to the scalar coordinates v_i for the requested k clusters. Degree-proportional initialization is described, and multiple random initial vectors may supply several embedding coordinates. Section 2.4 prose instead writes signed differences; the absolute-change convention here is explicitly the pseudocode/implementation convention.

entries.name: Zeta merging
entries.definition: An agglomerative graph-clustering algorithm that selects the pair with the largest sum of conditional increases in average log-diagonal resolvent popularity.
entries.identity_notes: Zeta merging is the named Algorithm 1 component of Zhao and Tang’s Zell method. Its input is an already constructed weighted graph and initial partition; it does not prescribe the l-links initialization. It differs from path integral clustering, which averages all endpoint-to-endpoint resolvent entries rather than logarithms of diagonal entries. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 218 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 15 lines each in existing discovery/review context. Five neighboring native records and five exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges were inspected.
limitations: Initialization, graph weights, damping and requested count determine the result; greedy merges cannot undo an initial grouping or certify a global partition optimum.

The paper prints z<rho(W) in Theorem 1, whereas the cycle power series requires |z|rho(W)<1. This record uses the stricter positive norm bound actually stated for Algorithm 1, rather than importing the printed general condition.

The printed bound 0<chi_C<=epsilon_C/|C| is not used. A two-vertex mutual-edge graph with z=1/4 gives chi_C=epsilon_C=log(16/15)>epsilon_C/2 under the paper’s own definitions; this is a curator counterexample, not an author erratum.

Zell’s full l-links and bandwidth conventions require separate clarification and are not specified by this component. No generic sparse-inverse runtime guarantee, automatic correct cluster count, or benchmark reproduction is asserted.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 2.2–3.2, PDF pp. 3–4, Equations (2)–(5), Theorem 2 and Algorithm 1; Section 4.3, pp. 5–6, component boundary

claims.statement: Given a fixed nonnegative weighted adjacency P, a nonempty initial partition and target count m_c smaller than its initial count, choose damping 0<z<1/(2||P||_1), the sufficient range stated in Section 3.1 for nonzero P. For a cluster C use the principal submatrix P_C without local renormalization and R_C=(I−zP_C)^−1. Its popularity is chi_C=(1/|C|) sum_(i in C) log (R_C)_ii. Equivalently it is the average leave-one-vertex-out reduction of epsilon_C=−log det(I−zP_C). For U=A union B, chi_(A|U) averages log (R_U)_ii over i in A with divisor |A|. Merge the current pair maximizing (chi_(A|U)−chi_A)+(chi_(B|U)−chi_B); recompute affected affinities and repeat to m_c. The conditional increment is not chi_U−chi_A−chi_B.

evidence.locator: Sections 2.2–3.2, PDF pp. 3–4, Equations (2)–(5), Theorem 2 and Algorithm 1; Section 4.3, pp. 5–6, component boundary

claims.statement: Curator calculation: for P=[[0,1],[1,0]], z=1/4 and C both vertices, det(I−zP)=15/16 and both diagonal entries of (I−zP)^−1 are 16/15. Thus epsilon_C=chi_C=log(16/15)>epsilon_C/2. The z choice satisfies Section 3.1’s sufficient norm bound. The printed upper bound after Theorem 2 is not adopted. The reproducible finite calculation is saved as research/discovery/zeta-popularity-bound.py; it is not a benchmark of the clustering procedure.

entries.name: CHAMELEON clustering
entries.definition: A graph-clustering procedure that first partitions a sparse neighbor graph into small subclusters and then agglomerates them using interconnectivity and closeness normalized by their internal bisection statistics.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the two-phase CHAMELEON procedure in Technical Report 99-007, including the two merge-selection alternatives described there. Dynamic modeling means recomputing cluster-relative graph statistics, not learning a neural representation. The inspected source is the 22-page report, not the eight-page final Computer article. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 218 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 15 lines each in existing discovery/review context. Five neighboring native records and five exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges were inspected.
limitations: Meaningful nonzero internal cut statistics and nonempty cross-edge sets are needed to evaluate the ratios. Very small or disconnected subclusters can make the estimates unstable or undefined; a zero-denominator policy is not supplied by this record.

Neighbor size, similarity, initial granularity, bisection balance and merge parameters influence results. The initial partition and later merges may cross desired cluster boundaries; the procedure does not establish semantic recovery.
The product-score and threshold-based schemes have different selection and stopping behavior; they are documented alternatives within the original named procedure, not assumed identical algorithms.

Internal cuts are computed by graph-partitioning software; describing the min-cut objective does not certify a global exact cut solver. Runtime depends in part on neighbor search and data dimension. No implementation or reported benchmark was reproduced.

definition_evidence.locator: Technical Report 99-007, Sections 4.1–4.4, printed pp. 5–11 (PDF pp. 6–12), Equations (1)–(4)

claims.statement: Construct a weighted undirected k-nearest-neighbor graph by retaining an edge when either endpoint lists the other among its k most similar points. Obtain small initial subclusters by repeated balanced graph bisection, selecting the largest current subcluster; the report uses hMETIS with each child holding at least 25 percent of its parent and stops when the largest subcluster is below MINSIZE. For clusters A,B, relative interconnectivity RI is the total cross-edge weight divided by the mean of the two internal bisection-cut weights. Relative closeness RC is the mean cross-edge weight divided by the size-weighted mean of the two mean internal bisection-edge weights. One merge scheme maximizes RI(A,B)*RC(A,B)^alpha over pairs; this is the scheme used for the report’s dendrogram experiments. An alternative visits clusters and selects their most strongly connected eligible neighbor subject to separate RI and RC thresholds, permitting multiple merges per iteration and either stopping or relaxing thresholds when no pair qualifies.

entries.name: Multi-class N-pair loss
entries.definition: A supervised metric-learning objective that averages a joint positive-versus-multiple-negative log-softmax loss across a batch of positive pairs drawn from distinct classes.
entries.identity_notes: This is Sohn’s N-pair-mc objective, Equation (7), together with its distinct-class positive-pair batching. The source also uses unqualified N-pair loss for a family including N-pair-ovo, so that family name is not an exact alias of this member. Its per-anchor categorical form is shared with generic InfoNCE at dot-product scores, but the named supervised batching configuration is retained explicitly. It is not the full SimCLR procedure or NT-Xent’s cosine-temperature two-view construction. N-pair-ovo instead sums individual pairwise softplus terms. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 218 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 15 lines each in existing discovery/review context. Five neighboring native records and five exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges were inspected.
limitations: Use N positive pairs from N distinct classes; other positive-side examples must represent different classes for the stated objective. Pair sampling and class selection are part of this configuration, not interchangeable with arbitrary augmented-view negatives.

The main paper uses embedding-norm regularization instead of a hard unit-length constraint. This record specifies the loss term; it does not prescribe a regularization coefficient, encoder, optimizer or full training schedule.

No unconditional equivalence to a margin triplet hinge or an information lower bound is asserted. Objective shape and label-based batching do not establish downstream accuracy. No training or benchmark was reproduced.

The proceedings Supplemental.zip inspected during retrieval contains a different paper by Steinhardt and Liang. It is not supporting evidence; this record relies on the inspected nine-page N-pair main paper.

definition_evidence.locator: Sections 3.1–3.2.2, PDF pp. 3–5; Equations (3) and (7), footnotes 1–2, embedding regularization discussion

claims.statement: Take N>=2 classes and two examples (x_i,x_i+) from each class. Encode 2N examples to f_i and f_i+. The Equation (7) objective is L_mc=(1/N) sum_i log[1+sum_(j!=i) exp(f_i^T f_j+−f_i^T f_i+)]. Each anchor has its paired positive and N−1 negative candidates from the positive side of other classes. Sharing these candidates across anchors forms N tuplets using 2N forward embeddings. Equation (7) specifies one orientation; footnote 2 also mentions a symmetric loss that swaps the anchor/positive roles, without specifying its aggregation in that footnote. No explicit temperature or cosine normalization appears in this expression.

entries.name: One-vs-one N-pair loss
entries.definition: A supervised metric-learning objective that sums separate positive-versus-negative softplus comparisons for each anchor in a batch of positive pairs from distinct classes.
entries.identity_notes: This is the named N-pair-ovo objective in Sohn’s Equation (8). It shares the N-pair batch construction with N-pair-mc but uses a sum of binary softplus comparisons, not one joint log-sum-exp over negatives. They coincide for one negative per anchor (N=2), but generally differ for N>2. No normalized identity match was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 218 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. Word-delimited fixed-string searches of both full checkouts, including ignored and hidden files, returned 15 lines each in existing discovery/review context. Five neighboring native records and five exact AIO nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges were inspected.
limitations: Use N positive pairs from N distinct classes; other positive-side examples must represent different classes for the stated objective. Pair sampling and class selection are part of this configuration, not interchangeable with arbitrary augmented-view negatives.

The main paper uses embedding-norm regularization instead of a hard unit-length constraint. This record specifies the loss term; it does not prescribe a regularization coefficient, encoder, optimizer or full training schedule.

No unconditional equivalence to a margin triplet hinge or an information lower bound is asserted. Objective shape and label-based batching do not establish downstream accuracy. No training or benchmark was reproduced.

The proceedings Supplemental.zip inspected during retrieval contains a different paper by Steinhardt and Liang. It is not supporting evidence; this record relies on the inspected nine-page N-pair main paper.

definition_evidence.locator: Section 3.2, PDF p. 4, Equations (7)–(8); Section 3.2.2, p. 5, regularization discussion

claims.statement: Given N>=2 positive pairs (x_i,x_i+) from N distinct classes and embeddings f_i,f_i+, define L_ovo=(1/N) sum_i sum_(j!=i) log[1+exp(f_i^T f_j+−f_i^T f_i+)]. Other positive-side examples supply N−1 different-class negatives to each anchor. The printed divisor is N, not N(N−1), so it averages across anchors while summing each anchor’s pairwise comparisons. In contrast, N-pair-mc places the sum over negatives inside a single logarithm. The expression uses dot products without an explicit temperature or cosine normalization.

Section2.4 defines signed velocity delta=v_t−v_(t−1), whereas Algorithm1 uses absolute component changes. Paper experimental threshold1e−5/n. Original author MATLAB pic.m uses dt=abs(vt−vtp), max(abs(dt−dtp)) and maximum iterations; nonnegative input makes sum normalization agree withL1. x_clusterembed_icml2010.m sets baseconv=.001 and maxit5000, i.e. threshold100 times the paper setting. These are source differences, not proof of runtime failure. Code was read but not executed. Constant initialization on a regular graph and negative eigenmodes/graph connectivity limit an unqualified guarantee. No benchmark claims or general convergence certificate planned.

zell2008.notes: Zell combines l-links initialization, row-normalized directed neighbor graph and Zeta merging. Eq3 epsilon_C=−logdet(I−zW_C); popularity is average leave-one-out epsilon reduction, equivalently average log diagonal resolvent. Conditional union popularity keeps original cluster index subset and1/|C| factor; Eq5 mergeaffinity=sumconditionalincrements, not simply total union minusparts. Algorithm1 gives sufficient0<z<1/(2||P||1). Several source inconsistencies need qualification or full-version/code checks before records: Theorem1 p3 prints z<rho(W) rather than reciprocal-radius convergence condition; p5 claims rho(P)<1 immediately before row-normalization (a nonnegative row-stochastic matrix has eigenvalue1); p3 popularity bound chi<=epsilon/n appears reversed for a two-node symmetric example; p5 prose says l message-passing steps while Algorithm2 starts with singleton and stops at |Ci|>=l. No arithmetic counterexample executed yet. Only3–5 coremethods read; rest full-paper/author resources remain to inspect. Subsequently readPDF6: component can use other initializers, and automatic-count heuristic fails on one displayed example. Re-read3–5 formulas. Executed an original exact-rational/two-node arithmetic calculation disproving the printed chi upper bound; preserved the source norm-bound convention. Full Zell/l-links remains pending because prose/Algorithm2 disagree on link count and Algorithm3 geometric-mean prose does not match its printed bandwidth factor. Row normalization gives spectral radius1, not the printed strict inequality. No universal replacement theorem asserted.
